displayName: HBM War of Civilizations Content Taxonomy
description: Conservative Phase 4 classification of exported HBM content. This taxonomy prepares review artifacts and inactive draft profiles; it is not a gameplay policy.
source: Phase 1 deterministic CSV inventory plus reviewed HBM registration and recipe patterns at checkpoint 63929fb4a.

families.description: Conventional projectile firearms reviewed for possible replacement by an external gun mod.
families.rationale: Exact item membership and exact recipe-output registry names are derived from the conventional-caliber Sedna source factories. They prevent the gun_ prefix from capturing launchers, energy weapons, powered tools, debug infrastructure, and unusual ammunition systems.
notes: Draft replacement only; keep active until a replacement mod is integrated and tested.

families.description: Ordinary bullet and shell metadata bands from ammo_standard, excluding explosive, rocket, flame, energy, nuclear, mortar, and utility variants.
families.rationale: All 55 exact metadata keys were reviewed against GunFactory.EnumAmmo. Recipe-output selectors are separate so item rules and crafting rows are not conflated.
notes: B75, explosive/white-phosphorus shells, flares, grenades, rockets, flame fuel, capacitors, coil, nuclear, HE, climbing, and mortar metadata are excluded.

families.description: Source-reviewed B75, explosive, white-phosphorus, and high-explosive EnumAmmo metadata outside the conventional replacement boundary.
families.rationale: Exact EnumAmmo ordinals keep explosive and special-purpose loads out of the ordinary small-arms ammunition replacement boundary.
notes: Descriptive classification only.

families.description: Source-reviewed flare, 40 mm grenade, and rocket EnumAmmo metadata outside the conventional firearm boundary.
families.rationale: Exact EnumAmmo ordinals separate launcher munitions from bullets and ordinary shotgun shells.
notes: Descriptive classification only.

families.description: Source-reviewed flamethrower and chemical-projector EnumAmmo metadata outside the conventional firearm boundary.
families.rationale: Exact EnumAmmo ordinals identify fuel and chemical-projector ammunition rather than ordinary small-arms rounds.
notes: Descriptive classification only.

families.description: Source-reviewed capacitor, energy-cell, coil, and tau EnumAmmo metadata outside the conventional firearm boundary.
families.rationale: Exact EnumAmmo ordinals identify non-ballistic energy systems.
notes: Descriptive classification only.

families.description: Source-reviewed nuclear and exotic nuclear EnumAmmo metadata outside the conventional firearm boundary.
families.rationale: Exact EnumAmmo ordinals provide nuclear evidence; naming or exporter categories alone do not.
notes: Descriptive classification only; no Phase 4 enforcement.

families.description: Source-reviewed climbing, mortar, and utility EnumAmmo metadata outside the conventional firearm boundary.
families.rationale: Exact EnumAmmo ordinals separate climbing and mortar utility loads from ordinary small-arms ammunition.
notes: Descriptive classification only.

families.description: Conventional hand grenades and dynamite-like explosive items.
families.rationale: Explosives remain HBM content and are not part of the firearm replacement draft.
notes: Research annotation is descriptive only.

families.description: Source-reviewed planted C4, Semtex, dynamite, explosive charges, and NTM TNT block/item/recipe forms.
families.rationale: Exact registry-name membership prevents conventional demolition explosives from inheriting nuclear semantics from their Java package or exporter category.
notes: Not part of the conventional firearm replacement profile.

families.description: Mining charges, mining detonators, and detonation cord used as demolition infrastructure.
families.rationale: These exact entries are industrial demolition tools, not nuclear weapons.

families.description: The fireworks block/item/recipe forms.
families.rationale: Fireworks are pyrotechnic content and must not inherit weapon.nuclear from blocks.bomb.

families.description: Missile items, missile entities, and missile launcher infrastructure.
families.rationale: Missiles are strategic project candidates and are intentionally excluded from the firearm replacement draft.
notes: No runtime project lock exists in Phase 4.

families.description: Nuclear weapon items, strategic warheads, and nuclear explosive blocks.
families.rationale: Reviewed membership is limited to the stable nuke_ device block namespace and exact source-proven nuclear launchers, demolition charge, and landmine. The generic blocks.bomb exporter category is explicitly not evidence of nuclear content.
notes: Descriptive only; Phase 3 does not enforce PROJECT_LOCKED.
Starter kits named hbm:item.nuke_* are intentionally excluded because they are kits, not weapons.

families.description: Laser, Tesla, coil, tau, and similar prototype gun-prefixed items.
families.rationale: Source factory assignments and exact item membership verify that these are energy or capacitor-based weapons rather than conventional ballistic firearms. Future acquisition policy remains descriptive and unenforced.
notes: Reviewed family membership does not approve EVENT_ONLY enforcement.

families.description: Source-reviewed flare and 40 mm launcher weapons excluded from the conventional small-arms replacement boundary.
families.rationale: These exact weapons consume flare or 40 mm grenade configurations, not conventional small-arms ammunition.
notes: Explicitly excluded from the conventional firearms profile.

families.description: Flamethrower and chemical-projector items and their recipe outputs.
families.rationale: Source factories show fuel/fluid projection rather than conventional cartridge firearms.
notes: Explicitly excluded from the conventional firearms profile.

families.description: Secret 35-800 weapons and the 75-caliber bolter using unusual ammunition systems.
families.rationale: Exact source factories use secret or 75-caliber special ammunition and are outside the conventional replacement contract.
notes: Explicitly excluded from the conventional firearms profile.

families.description: Utility devices implemented through the Sedna gun framework plus gun repair kits.
families.rationale: Source classes and factories prove these are tools, powered-armor devices, extinguishers, mortar/line tools, or repair kits rather than replacement-target firearms.
notes: Explicitly excluded from the conventional firearms profile.

families.description: Blades, swords, and close-combat utility weapons retained as HBM content.
families.rationale: These entries are not conventional firearm replacements.

families.description: HBM armor registration category, excluding narrower hazmat matches by selector precedence.
families.rationale: The source category is stable, but power armor, inserts, jetpacks, masks, and ordinary armor need subfamily review.
notes: Never included in the no-HBM-conventional-firearms draft.

families.description: Hazmat-prefixed protective gear.
families.rationale: Foundational protective equipment must remain available for world and reactor safety.

families.description: Minecart and train entities that may later integrate with a dedicated vehicle mod.
families.rationale: HBM does not expose one clean vehicle registry; only narrow entity patterns are classified.
notes: Phase 4 does not implement or remove vehicles.

families.description: Ore blocks and ore-form item outputs.
families.rationale: Foundational world and processing inputs are explicitly retained.
notes: This content family is separate from the unsupported worldgen-ore generator family.

families.description: Common ingot, plate, powder, nugget, and billet forms.
families.rationale: Material forms remain foundational even when future research describes their production.

families.description: Reviewed schrabidium, euphemium, and dineutronium material forms.
families.rationale: Advanced materials are descriptive research candidates, not Phase 4 runtime locks.

families.description: Uranium, plutonium, thorium, polonium, radium, and nuclear fuel material forms.
families.rationale: Nuclear forms require future nation-owned research review but are never safe mass-disable candidates.

families.description: Machine components, mechanical parts, and machine plates.
families.rationale: Foundational components remain present; future research may describe production access.

families.description: Wire, coil, motor, and electrical component forms.
families.rationale: Stable prefix classification for electrical forms.

families.description: Circuit, board, and electronic control components.
families.rationale: Stable registry-name forms identify electronic components.

families.description: Reactor control, fuel, and nuclear machine components.
families.rationale: Nuclear component access is future research metadata only.

families.description: Solid, liquid, and gaseous conventional fuel items and fluids selected by stable names.
families.rationale: Foundational fuels remain available; fluid names are exact because process intent cannot be inferred broadly.

families.description: RBMK fuel and fuel-rod forms.
families.rationale: Nuclear fuel is a future nation-ledger research candidate but remains present and unenforced.

families.description: Waste items and explicitly named waste fluids.
families.rationale: Wastes are required for safe process accounting and are not removal candidates.

families.description: A conservative exact set of common industrial chemical fluids.
families.rationale: Exact membership avoids inferring purpose for every HBM fluid.
notes: Other fluids remain unresolved until process-context review.

families.description: Exported machine recipes plus stable processing-machine block prefixes.
families.rationale: Phase 4 preserves all supported machine recipe systems; narrower machine families may add compatible tags.
notes: Multipurpose machines require later subfamily review; this family is not approved for disabling.

families.description: Generators, turbines, batteries, and power-production machine blocks.
families.rationale: Power infrastructure is foundational and remains active.

families.description: RBMK, reactor, pile, and nuclear-process machine content.
families.rationale: Future research annotations describe access without removing world-loading tile entities.
notes: Never mass-disable nuclear machines.

families.description: Conveyors, cranes, and transfer infrastructure.
families.rationale: Logistics infrastructure is retained and may later expose narrow modifier hooks.

families.description: Crates, barrels, tanks, and storage machines.
families.rationale: Storage is foundational and unsafe to remove from existing worlds.

families.description: Turrets, radar, and launch-control machine content.
families.rationale: Military machines remain HBM-owned; research metadata is descriptive.
notes: Never included in the no-HBM-conventional-firearms draft.

families.description: Decoration, brick, concrete, and asphalt block forms.
families.rationale: Decorative content is retained.

families.description: Items registered in HBM's food source category.
families.rationale: Stable exporter category identifies food.

families.description: Syringes, medkits, bandages, and radiation medicine.
families.rationale: Medical and radiation-survival content remains available.

families.description: The broad HBM tool source category, retained as an explicit unresolved review bucket.
families.rationale: The source category mixes diagnostics, utility devices, ammo storage, and weapon-like tools; it must not be guessed into narrower families.

families.description: Reserved family for ore generator records; the current exporter does not emit ore-generation features.
families.rationale: A zero expansion is intentional and documents the exporter coverage gap without inventing records.
notes: Do not treat ore blocks as proof of ore-generator coverage.

families.description: All named weighted NBT structure features emitted by the Phase 1 exporter.
families.rationale: Named structures remain enabled; taxonomy does not mutate world generation.
notes: Coordinate-predicate structures remain a Phase 3 enforcement limitation.

families.description: All exported HBM ItemPool structure-loot occurrences.
families.rationale: Loot records remain enabled; item-family tags do not imply loot-removal policy.
notes: Non-ItemPool loot is not universally exported or enforced.

families.description: Exact confirmed developer-only items, blocks, and entities.
families.rationale: Only exact keys confirmed from development registrations are eligible for the server draft's DISABLED state.
notes: Phase 3 currently enforces only supported content kinds; entity DISABLED remains descriptive.

families.description: Exact undefined sentinel content requiring administrative review.
families.rationale: Sentinel names are strong evidence but not sufficient to activate removal in Phase 4.

families.description: Exact creative power sources and creative machine variants.
families.rationale: Creative-only content is retained as admin/event-only metadata and is not disabled in Phase 4.
notes: Phase 3 does not enforce EVENT_ONLY.

exactOverrides.rationale: Explicit Phase 4 review confirms the event tester block is development-only.
Explicit Phase 4 review confirms the event tester item form is development-only.
Explicit Phase 4 review confirms the object tester block is development-only.
Explicit Phase 4 review confirms the object tester item form is development-only.

notes: Selectors are conjunctive within an object and ORed within a family.
Exact overrides beat explicit family membership, which beats narrow selectors, broad selectors, the taxonomy default, and unresolved fallback.
No generated profile is activated automatically.
Heuristic suggestions are disabled by default and may never become reviewed automatically.
